source.title: Tilting the playing field: Dynamical loss functions for machine learning
source.authors: M. Ruiz-García; Ge Zhang; S. Schoenholz; Andrea J. Liu

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary materials are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether gradient training reaches high training accuracy under static and dynamically changing loss functions, including a CIFAR-10 network and a narrow synthetic-data network. Its intervention differs from the versions’ recipes.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own training-accuracy outcomes under static and oscillatory loss. Other reported results about validation/test accuracy and Hessian/NTK dynamics do not directly measure a claim version's training classification behavior and are not included. Cited findings from other studies are not recorded as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own training accuracy for a randomly initialized convolutional network on CIFAR-10, directly bearing on V1. Its main intervention changes the loss during training. The spiral experiments and curvature analyses do not test the specific systems and conditions named in the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the optimization conclusion, but omits a major conclusion: cyclic class weighting can also improve generalization in overparameterized networks. The authors demonstrate these benefits in selected settings and report no statistically significant test-accuracy improvement for their Wide Residual Network experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a time-varying class-weighted loss; also evaluates standard static cross-entropy as a comparison. It does not test the cited claim's random-label or CIFAR-100 settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Training outcome differs with network width and loss choice: the 100-unit spiral model has ∼ 0.65 training accuracy under static loss but nearly perfect accuracy in a region under oscillatory loss; the 1000-unit model has ∼ 1 under static loss. CIFAR-10 Myrtle5 reaches ∼ 1 under static loss.

fits_no_version.finding: On spiral data, static-loss training reaches approximately 0.65 accuracy with 100 hidden units and approximately 1 with 1000 units; favorable oscillatory losses enable nearly perfect accuracy in the narrow network.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width and cyclic class weighting can determine whether a one-hidden-layer network fits synthetic spiral data under a fixed training budget and learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: With dynamically weighted cross-entropy, curvature crossing a learning-rate-dependent threshold produces bifurcation cascades; the illustrated narrow network eventually reaches valleys that remain below threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cyclic changes to class weights can induce temporary curvature-driven instabilities that help gradient descent reach wider valleys.

record.problems: The Myrtle5 CIFAR-10 training-accuracy phase diagram is figure-only. The spiral-data outcomes are averaged over 50 simulations, but no uncertainty is stated. The CIFAR-10 setup uses 64 channels; the paper does not test random or corrupted labels or CIFAR-100.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows were required for the claim versions tested. The paper's test/validation accuracy and Hessian/NTK results do not directly measure the training-classification behavior specified by these versions.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; Adam; controlled comparisons of model size, early stopping, and regularization. Oscillatory CIFAR-10 training accuracy cannot be resolved from the supplied figure transcription.
ReLU teacher-student problems, verified spurious local minima, and the effect of adding one or two student neurons within the specified widths.
Training-error comparisons across depth, identity shortcuts, and the special initialization exceptions.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, signal or gradient preservation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit in wide squared-loss networks, divergence at larger rates, sustained edge-of-stability training, and divergence from initially subthreshold runs.
Controlled comparisons with and without batch normalization, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version. Synthetic spiral results warrant no V1 scope limitation because they lie outside its stated architecture and datasets. The curvature results use a changing cross-entropy objective and do not establish V5's specified stability-limit behavior. Figure values unavailable in the supplied text were not inferred.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, SGD/Adam comparison, or the effects of smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
